newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swissair, Sabena discuss German freight merger.
newsitem.headline: Swissair, Sabena discuss German freight merger.

text.p: The Belgian airline Sabena and the Swiss airline Swissair are discussing merging their German freight capacities, a spokeswoman for Sabena said on Tueday.
"The prospect of Swissair taking over Sabena's freight business is being discussed," the spokeswoman said, but she added that no decision had yet been reached.
However, Sabena had no intention of closing its passenger business in Germany, the spokeswoman said, denying rumours that Sabena was considering closing its sales offices in Germany.
Sabena would not say how big its German freight business was. Any merger in the freight business would affect three offices in Germany.
Swissair owns 49.5 percent of Sabena. In October Swissair announced that it would take over the marketing of Sabena's freight business from the start of 1997.
This increased Swissair's cargo capacity by 25 percent.
